system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild
T5: Claiming Terraform authoring
T6: The old cover letter is addressed to his current employer: writer must not reuse its 'Insurance is new to me' framing

Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and running Java/Spring Boot services for insurance and
travel products. Experience in REST API design, Kafka event processing, relational databases and query
tuning, automated testing, and AWS EKS deployments. Combines measurable API performance improvements
with regular production on-call responsibility.
Professional Experience
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Jan 2022 - Present
• Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.

Event-driven integration: Kafka, RabbitMQ, idempotent consumers, outbox pattern

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Email: daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | Phone: +351 555 010 202
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example
Tessel Cargo Software
Hiring Team, Routing & Tracking
Application: Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform
Dear Hiring Team,
Your Routing & Tracking team’s challenge of turning carrier events into reliable live tracking
closely matches the backend problems I have worked on: reliable event processing, API
performance and production operation. I bring 7 years of backend engineering experience in
insurance and travel. My production background is in Java and Spring Boot, matching the
comparable-language experience your advertisement welcomes.
At Tejo Insurance Tech, I develop and maintain seven microservices for policy quoting and
claims intake. For our Kafka-based claims workflow, I introduced idempotent consumers and
an outbox table that eliminated duplicate claim records. I also designed the partner quoting
REST API used by 12 broker partners and reduced its quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8
seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query improvements. These are
directly relevant foundations for dependable carrier-event ingestion and a responsive public
tracking API.
My experience also covers the operational side of backend delivery. I deploy services to AWS
EKS using Helm and Jenkins pipelines and take production on-call responsibility one week per
month. Previously, at Viajar Online, I wrote Testcontainers integration tests that increased
payments module coverage from 35% to 70% and helped extract a Spring Boot notifications
service from a monolith. Alongside PostgreSQL, Oracle and Docker skills, this provides a
practical foundation for your team’s database, automated testing and cloud deployment work.
Tessel’s emphasis on clean APIs and engineers owning what they run aligns with my focus on
API quality and production reliability. I would welcome a conversation about how my
experience with event-driven services, performance tuning and operational responsibility could
contribute to Tessel Track.
Kind regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
